= Statement of Work: Systemd Orchestration Refactoring
:author: AI Assistant + Human Collaborator
:revdate: 2026-02-08
:toc: left
:toclevels: 3
:icons: font

== Context

We are evolving the custom systemd orchestration for the RKE2Lab environment. The current implementation has:

* Inconsistent naming conventions (`*-manifests-install.service` vs `*-manifests.service`)
* Separate ready-check services that could be integrated into manifests services
* Target files that only wait for a single service (providing no value)
* Recent changes include prefixed unit names to avoid collisions with upstream RKE2
* Flox/Nix build flow adjustments

The architecture has grown organically and needs systematic refactoring for clarity and maintainability.

== Objectives

. Standardize naming conventions across all systemd units and scripts
. Integrate readiness checks into manifests services as post-start behaviors
. Eliminate redundant targets when only one service contributes to a "stage"
. Simplify dependency graphs while preserving boot ordering guarantees
. Keep documentation and activation scripts aligned with new conventions
. Reduce total line count and number of files while maintaining functionality

== Scope

=== In Scope

* Custom systemd units and targets installed by this repository
* Associated scripts invoked by those units  
* Documentation describing boot flow and systemd architecture
* Activation scripts that enable/start units

=== Out of Scope

* Upstream `rke2-server.service` and `rke2-agent.service` definitions
* Non-systemd runtime components not managed by these units
* Unrelated docs and packages outside the custom systemd layer
* The `rke2lab-flox-builds-complete.target` (truly independent/parallel)

== Assumptions

* The RKE2 server/agent units remain the authoritative upstream services
* Custom units are deployed via bind mounts and activation scripts
* The cluster uses the rke2lab-prefixed unit naming moving forward
* Fail-fast behavior for readiness checks must be preserved
* Boot ordering must remain correct (no regressions)

== Approach

The work is divided into phases for systematic execution:

=== link:phase1-inventory.adoc[Phase 1: Inventory & Mapping]

Create comprehensive inventory of all systemd units, scripts, and their dependencies.
Map current names to proposed new names. Document dependency chains.

=== link:phase2-naming-refactor.adoc[Phase 2: Naming Refactor]

Systematically rename all units and scripts to follow standardized conventions:

* `*-manifests-install.service` → `*-manifests.service`
* `*-ready-check.service` → `*-ready.service`  
* `*-ready-check.sh` → `*-ready.sh`

Update all references across services, targets, scripts, and documentation.

=== link:phase3-readiness-integration.adoc[Phase 3: Readiness Integration & Simplification]

* Move readiness checks from separate services into `ExecStartPost` of manifests services
* Eliminate redundant ready services
* Evaluate and remove targets that only wait for one service
* Convert to direct service dependencies (clearer and simpler)
* Update documentation to reflect new architecture

=== Phase 4: Validation

* Verify systemd unit graph is coherent
* Test on actual cluster deployment
* Confirm readiness checks still run and fail appropriately
* Validate boot ordering and timing

== Deliverables

. *Updated Unit Files*
** 8 manifests services renamed
** 5 ready services eliminated (integrated into manifests)
** 6 targets eliminated (redundant single-service targets)
** Updated dependency declarations

. *Updated Scripts*
** 3 readiness check scripts renamed
** Activation script updated with new service names

. *Updated Documentation*
** Revised architecture documentation (systemd-service-architecture.adoc)
** Updated diagrams showing simplified flow
** Examples and debugging guidance reflecting new structure

. *Inventory & Mapping*
** Complete inventory of all units and scripts
** Mapping of old → new names
** Dependency chain documentation

== Acceptance Criteria

✅ *Correctness*

* [x] All systemd units load without errors

✅ *Simplification*

* [x] Net reduction in lines of code

* [x] Direct dependencies replace target indirection
* [x] One service per layer (no separate ready services)

✅ *Documentation*

* [x] Architecture docs match implementation
* [x] Examples and diagrams updated

* [x] Debugging commands reference correct units

✅ *Maintainability*

* [x] Git history preserved through renames
* [x] Naming conventions followed consistently

* [x] Future additions have clear patterns to follow

== Results Summary

.*Phase 2 Results*

.*Phase 3 Results*
* 5 ready services eliminated (integrated into manifests)
* 6 targets eliminated (redundant)

* Direct service dependencies replacing targets

.*Overall Impact*
* Files changed: 30
* Files renamed: 8 (services) + 3 (scripts) = 11

* Simplification ratio: ~30% fewer systemd-related files

== Remote Execution Pattern

Use this command pattern to run commands on the NixOS VM and inside the Incus node:

[source,bash]
----
ssh <host>-nixos.local -- incus exec <node> -- flox activate --dir=/var/lib/rancher/rke2 -- <cmd>
----

.Examples
[source,bash]
----
# Check nodes
ssh bioskop-nixos.local -- incus exec master -- flox activate --dir=/var/lib/rancher/rke2 -- kubectl get nodes

# Check service status  
ssh bioskop-nixos.local -- incus exec master -- systemctl status rke2lab-mesh-manifests.service
----

== Host Orchestration Conventions

* On the NixOS VM, activate flox in the rke2lab working tree before orchestration:
+
[source,bash]
----
ssh <host>-nixos.local -- flox activate --dir=/var/lib/git/nxmatic/rke2lab -- <cmd>
----

* Always use `remake` (not `make`) for deployment orchestration
